limitations:
Read verified campaign artifacts. No analyzer, JVM, build, or profile process is started.
Packet counts are exact events, not retained facts. Census rows are end-state annotations.
CPU deltas interpolate one-second /proc process samples; they are not CPU-stack shares.
Loop-method diagnostics cover at most 24 completed owners; aborted owners are the union of two top-12 samples.
N2 selectedCall*/persistedReplay* describe physical inter-method calls. Local BlockSummaryLinks do not increment those service counters.
START-to-END arithmetic differences include gauges/peaks; only cumulative counter fields mean event work. Peak/gauge changes must not be reported as work avoided.
New census admitted/outgoing includes public+internal rows; publicAdmitted/publicOutgoing subtract the separately logged block census.

An unfinished run has no frozen completed body/census; BODY_WORK_STATISTICS snapshotActors=0 from an aborted RunResult is not zero performed work. Aborted hot-owner steps are stopped-owner evidence, not a complete frontier.
End-state store counts, cumulative events, sampled allocation churn, RSS, and retained heap are different measurements.
Equal run index/direction/limit is necessary for workload comparison; changed scoped frontiers mean equal inputs/work are not guaranteed.

message.text:
A trust boundary can be thought of as line drawn through a program. On one side
of the line, data is untrusted. On the other side of the line, data is assumed
to be trustworthy. The purpose of validation logic is to allow data to safely
cross the trust boundary - to move from untrusted to trusted. A trust boundary
violation occurs when a program blurs the line between what is trusted and what
is untrusted. By combining trusted and untrusted data in the same data
structure, it becomes easier for programmers to mistakenly trust unvalidated
data.

prior1e6Comparison.interpretation: Only the formerly missing BenchmarkTest01875 sink is added; the4111prioridentities remain.

gc.qualification: Whole-process counts include initialization, prescan and teardown. Phase attribution uses GC completion timestamps; a pause crossing a boundary is not split. These are pause durations, not concurrent-GC CPU shares, allocation volume, object ownership, or retained dominator size.

normalExitGapEvidence.coverage: This is a sample of logged original method owners, not an all-method layout census. Completed runs log at most 24 loop owners ranked by steps; aborted runs log the union of the top 12 by steps and top 12 by candidate offers (at most 24 owners, possibly fewer loop owners). maxLoggedGapsPerOwner is the maximum certificate count among logged owners only. A zero maximum or no nonzero logged rows does not prove that all layouts have no gaps. Repeated owner rows in different runs describe the same structural program layout, not new loops. Each positive certificate is a layout qualification: no common normal exit was certified; the analyzer retains original physical routes. This reader never selects a replacement target.

caveats: Preexisting does not mean acceptable, false positive, or fixed. The strict f945 gate still records every missing identity.
Trace multiplicity and code-flow counts do not define sink identity; complete occurrence rows remain evidence.
Same method/rule at another return is not an automatic replacement for a missing fingerprint.
Historical source evidence is reused as a documented mechanism, not presented as a new measured runtime lineage.
Latest run labels here come from the command summary; cross-check exact positive engine/report markers for final acceptance.

limitations:
Read verified campaign artifacts. No analyzer, JVM, build, or profile process is started.
Packet counts are exact events, not retained facts. Census rows are end-state annotations.
CPU deltas interpolate one-second /proc process samples; they are not CPU-stack shares.
Loop-method diagnostics cover at most 24 completed owners; aborted owners are the union of two top-12 samples.
N2 selectedCall*/persistedReplay* describe physical inter-method calls. Local BlockSummaryLinks do not increment those service counters.
START-to-END arithmetic differences include gauges/peaks; only cumulative counter fields mean event work. Peak/gauge changes must not be reported as work avoided.
New census admitted/outgoing includes public+internal rows; publicAdmitted/publicOutgoing subtract the separately logged block census.

An unfinished run has no frozen completed body/census; BODY_WORK_STATISTICS snapshotActors=0 from an aborted RunResult is not zero performed work. Aborted hot-owner steps are stopped-owner evidence, not a complete frontier.
End-state store counts, cumulative events, sampled allocation churn, RSS, and retained heap are different measurements.
Equal run index/direction/limit is necessary for workload comparison; changed scoped frontiers mean equal inputs/work are not guaranteed.

gc.qualification: Whole-process counts include initialization, prescan and teardown. Phase attribution uses GC completion timestamps; a pause crossing a boundary is not split. These are pause durations, not concurrent-GC CPU shares, allocation volume, object ownership, or retained dominator size.

normalExitGapEvidence.coverage: This is a sample of logged original method owners, not an all-method layout census. Completed runs log at most 24 loop owners ranked by steps; aborted runs log the union of the top 12 by steps and top 12 by candidate offers (at most 24 owners, possibly fewer loop owners). maxLoggedGapsPerOwner is the maximum certificate count among logged owners only. A zero maximum or no nonzero logged rows does not prove that all layouts have no gaps. Repeated owner rows in different runs describe the same structural program layout, not new loops. Each positive certificate is a layout qualification: no common normal exit was certified; the analyzer retains original physical routes. This reader never selects a replacement target.

A zero maximum or no nonzero logged rows does not prove that all layouts have no gaps. Repeated owner rows in different runs describe the same structural program layout, not new loops. Each positive certificate is a layout qualification: no common normal exit was certified; the analyzer retains original physical routes. This reader never selects a replacement target.

limitations:
Read verified campaign artifacts. No analyzer, JVM, build, or profile process is started.
Packet counts are exact events, not retained facts. Census rows are end-state annotations.
CPU deltas interpolate one-second /proc process samples; they are not CPU-stack shares.
Loop-method diagnostics cover at most 24 completed owners; aborted owners are the union of two top-12 samples.
N2 selectedCall*/persistedReplay* describe physical inter-method calls. Local BlockSummaryLinks do not increment those service counters.
START-to-END arithmetic differences include gauges/peaks; only cumulative counter fields mean event work. Peak/gauge changes must not be reported as work avoided.
New census admitted/outgoing includes public+internal rows; publicAdmitted/publicOutgoing subtract the separately logged block census.

An unfinished run has no frozen completed body/census; BODY_WORK_STATISTICS snapshotActors=0 from an aborted RunResult is not zero performed work. Aborted hot-owner steps are stopped-owner evidence, not a complete frontier.
End-state store counts, cumulative events, sampled allocation churn, RSS, and retained heap are different measurements.
Equal run index/direction/limit is necessary for workload comparison; changed scoped frontiers mean equal inputs/work are not guaranteed.

rules:
  - id: java-unsafe-reflection-sinks
    options:
      lib: true
    tags:
      - unsafe-reflection-sink
    severity: NOTE
    message: Using reflection on user-manipulated name
    languages:
      - java
    pattern-either:
      - pattern: java.lang.Class.forName($UNTRUSTED,...)
      - pattern: java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke($UNTRUSTED,...)

rules:
  - id: spring-untrusted-data-source
    options:
      lib: true
    tags:
      - untrusted-data-source
    severity: NOTE
    message: Untrusted data flows from here
    metadata:
      short-description: Untrusted data source in Spring request handlers
      full-description: |-
        This is a source rule for untrusted input in Spring MVC / Spring Boot handlers.
        It marks method parameters and request-derived values as tainted when they can be
        controlled by an external caller.

        Typical source locations matched by this rule include:
        - Handler method parameters in `@RequestMapping`, `@GetMapping`, `@PostMapping`, etc.
        - Values returned by `MessageBodyReader.readFrom(...)`
        - Cookie values resolved via `WebUtils.getCookie(...).getValue()`

        Example source usage (tainted):

        ```java
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

        @RestController
        class SearchController {
            @GetMapping("/search")
            String search(@RequestParam String q) {
                // q is a source: untrusted user-controlled input
                return doSearch(q);
            }

            private String doSearch(String input) {
                // Vulnerability findings appear only when this value reaches an unsafe usage.
                return input;
            }
        }
        ```

        Recommended handling at the boundary:
        - Assume all request parameters, headers, cookies, and bodies are untrusted.
        - Apply validation constraints (Bean Validation / explicit checks) close to controller boundaries.
        - Normalize and map external input to typed internal models before unsafe usage.
    languages:
      - java
    patterns:
      - pattern-either:
          - patterns:
              - pattern: |
                  @$ANNOTATION(...)
                  $RETURNTYPE $METHODNAME(..., $TYPE $UNTRUSTED,...) {
                    ...
                  }
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $TYPE
                  regex: ^(?!(Integer|Long|Float|Double|Char|Boolean|int|long|float|double|char|boolean|BindingResult|HttpMethod|java.util.TimeZone|java.util.Locale|java.util.ZoneId))
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $ANNOTATION
                  patterns:
                    - pattern-either:
                        - pattern: RequestMapping
                        - pattern: DeleteMapping
                        - pattern: GetMapping
                        - pattern: PatchMapping
                        - pattern: PostMapping
                        - pattern: PutMapping
          - pattern: |
              $UNTRUSTED = (MessageBodyReader $READER).readFrom(...);
          - pattern: |

normalExitGaps.coverage: This is a sample of logged original method owners, not an all-method layout census. Completed runs log at most 24 loop owners ranked by steps; aborted runs log the union of the top 12 by steps and top 12 by candidate offers (at most 24 owners, possibly fewer loop owners). maxLoggedGapsPerOwner is the maximum certificate count among logged owners only. A zero maximum or no nonzero logged rows does not prove that all layouts have no gaps. Repeated owner rows in different runs describe the same structural program layout, not new loops. Each positive certificate is a layout qualification: no common normal exit was certified; the analyzer retains original physical routes. This reader never selects a replacement target.

limitations:
Read verified campaign artifacts. No analyzer, JVM, build, or profile process is started.
Packet counts are exact events, not retained facts. Census rows are end-state annotations.
CPU deltas interpolate one-second /proc process samples; they are not CPU-stack shares.
Loop-method diagnostics cover at most 24 completed owners; aborted owners are the union of two top-12 samples.
N2 selectedCall*/persistedReplay* describe physical inter-method calls. Local BlockSummaryLinks do not increment those service counters.
START-to-END arithmetic differences include gauges/peaks; only cumulative counter fields mean event work. Peak/gauge changes must not be reported as work avoided.
New census admitted/outgoing includes public+internal rows; publicAdmitted/publicOutgoing subtract the separately logged block census.

An unfinished run has no frozen completed body/census; BODY_WORK_STATISTICS snapshotActors=0 from an aborted RunResult is not zero performed work. Aborted hot-owner steps are stopped-owner evidence, not a complete frontier.
End-state store counts, cumulative events, sampled allocation churn, RSS, and retained heap are different measurements.
Equal run index/direction/limit is necessary for workload comparison; changed scoped frontiers mean equal inputs/work are not guaranteed.

gc.qualification: Whole-process counts include initialization, prescan and teardown. Phase attribution uses GC completion timestamps; a pause crossing a boundary is not split. These are pause durations, not concurrent-GC CPU shares, allocation volume, object ownership, or retained dominator size.

rules:
  - id: command-injection-sinks
    options:
      lib: true
    tags:
      - command-injection-sink
    severity: NOTE
    message: Executing OS command with user-controlled data
    metadata:
      provenance: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/security-products/sast-rules/-/blob/main/java/inject/rule-CommandInjection.yml
    languages:
      - java
    patterns:
      - pattern-either:
          - pattern: |
              (ProcessBuilder $PB).command(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
          - pattern:
              new ProcessBuilder(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
          - pattern:
              (java.util.List $ARGS).add($UNTRUSTED);
              ...
              new ProcessBuilder(..., $ARGS, ...);
          - pattern:
              (java.util.List $ARGS) = List.of(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
              ...
              new ProcessBuilder(..., $ARGS, ...);
          - pattern:
              (java.util.List $ARGS).add($UNTRUSTED);
              ...
              (ProcessBuilder $PB).command($ARGS);
          - pattern:
              (java.util.List $ARGS) = List.of(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
              ...
              (ProcessBuilder $PB).command($ARGS);
          - patterns:
              - pattern: |
                  (ProcessBuilder $PB).command().$ADD(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $ADD
                  regex: (add|addAll)
          - patterns:
              - pattern: |
                  (java.lang.Runtime $R).$EXEC(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...);
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $EXEC
                  regex: (exec|loadLibrary|load)

  - id: java-expression-language-sinks
    options:
      lib: true
    tags:
      - el-injection-sink
    severity: NOTE
    message: Java EL evaluation directly with user-supplied input
    metadata:
      provenance: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/security-products/sast-rules/-/blob/main/java/inject/rule-ELInjection.yml
    languages:
      - java
    pattern-either:
      - pattern: (ExpressionFactory $EXP).createValueExpression((ELContext $CTX), $UNTRUSTED, ...)
      - pattern: (ExpressionFactory $EXP).createMethodExpression((ELContext $CTX), $UNTRUSTED, ...)
      - pattern: $OBJECT.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate($UNTRUSTED, ...)
      - pattern: ($X.el.ELProcessor $P).eval(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...)
      - pattern: ($X.el.ELProcessor $P).getValue(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...)
      - pattern: ($X.el.ELProcessor $P).setValue(..., $UNTRUSTED, ...)

rules:
  - id: spring-untrusted-data-source
    options:
      lib: true
    tags:
      - untrusted-data-source
    severity: NOTE
    message: Untrusted data flows from here
    metadata:
      short-description: Untrusted data source in Spring request handlers
      full-description: |-
        This is a source rule for untrusted input in Spring MVC / Spring Boot handlers.
        It marks method parameters and request-derived values as tainted when they can be
        controlled by an external caller.

        Typical source locations matched by this rule include:
        - Handler method parameters in `@RequestMapping`, `@GetMapping`, `@PostMapping`, etc.
        - Values returned by `MessageBodyReader.readFrom(...)`
        - Cookie values resolved via `WebUtils.getCookie(...).getValue()`

        Example source usage (tainted):

        ```java
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
        import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

        @RestController
        class SearchController {
            @GetMapping("/search")
            String search(@RequestParam String q) {
                // q is a source: untrusted user-controlled input
                return doSearch(q);
            }

            private String doSearch(String input) {
                // Vulnerability findings appear only when this value reaches an unsafe usage.
                return input;
            }
        }
        ```

        Recommended handling at the boundary:
        - Assume all request parameters, headers, cookies, and bodies are untrusted.
        - Apply validation constraints (Bean Validation / explicit checks) close to controller boundaries.
        - Normalize and map external input to typed internal models before unsafe usage.
    languages:
      - java
    patterns:
      - pattern-either:
          - patterns:
              - pattern: |
                  @$ANNOTATION(...)
                  $RETURNTYPE $METHODNAME(..., $TYPE $UNTRUSTED,...) {
                    ...
                  }
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $TYPE
                  regex: ^(?!(Integer|Long|Float|Double|Char|Boolean|int|long|float|double|char|boolean|BindingResult|HttpMethod|java.util.TimeZone|java.util.Locale|java.util.ZoneId))
              - metavariable-pattern:
                  metavariable: $ANNOTATION
                  patterns:
                    - pattern-either:
                        - pattern: RequestMapping
                        - pattern: DeleteMapping
                        - pattern: GetMapping
                        - pattern: PatchMapping
                        - pattern: PostMapping
                        - pattern: PutMapping
          - pattern: |
              $UNTRUSTED = (MessageBodyReader $READER).readFrom(...);
          - pattern: |
              Cookie $COOKIE = org.springframework.web.util.WebUtils.getCookie(...);
              ...
              $UNTRUSTED = $COOKIE.getValue();

mechanism: JApplicationSingleExitGraph routes every ordinary return to one synthetic JMethodExitNormalInst.
JIRBoundaryForms resolves method-exit sinks at that shared exit; the report catalog identifies its statement, not its original per-return predecessor.
JIRBidiAnalysis converts report descriptors to TracePathGenerationResult.Simple, with no predecessor trace for the renderer.

JirSarifGenerator.statementLocation sees a generated boundary; TraceMessageBuilder.tryResolveExitLocation chooses a real exit from relevantLocations when present, otherwise the last matching return in the method instruction list.

The legacy baseline has a generated trace ending at the earlier return. The BDI SARIF has zero codeFlows and points to the final source return: Pipeline.catch return null at line130 (JIR109), and EML.catch IOException return at148-149 (JIR126).
reportingMechanism.conclusion: Source code and exact SARIF pairing support a representative-exit reporting-location explanation for the two missing strict return identities. They do not prove equal detection of the original per-return source-to-sink paths.

qualifications: ExecutionSample counts/shares describe sampled Java-thread stacks. Native GC/compiler CPU is absent. Collapsed CPU includes native stacks with its own all-sample denominator; no share is converted to wall/process CPU.
Allocation weight estimates allocation churn, not retained heap or exact allocation. Allocation callsite is the first bidi frame in the allocation stack.

Aborted/unequal windows are not comparable regression totals. Observed durations/rates are descriptive; even completed same-numbered iterations may execute different work or recover different findings.
R1 engine-body and run-1-static-completion are distinct disjoint split windows; exactRunMarkers retain the entire start/end marker span. IFDS aggregates overlap those phases and must not be summed.
Collapsed captures have no event timestamps. Exact observed CPU-window classification is reported; mixed captures are not assigned to their starting run or proportionally split.
Observer deep components choose the deepest matching semantic operation per observer sample. Component percentages use observer-only denominators and are not added to top-level scopes.

The6188-control direct-vs-streamed Stirling validation belongs to the historical1e6 recording only. It is implementation evidence, not a new validation of these050b recordings. The old validator was not run.
No JFR/heap file was read, no JVM/MAT/profiler/analyzer was started, and no verified reader/helper/pin receipt was edited by this helper.
Absent samples or unavailable derived fields are not evidence that an operation never occurs; inclusive frame/family percentages overlap.
